chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: Pittsburgh bassists, teacher Mr. Kelly, and musicians who doubled
summary: Frank Clarke and the school teacher Kelly produced Pittsburgh's bass players; musicians then doubled on several instruments, like Benny Carter.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And I worked with Roy --
Well, who else was in the band?
Well, Frank Clarke, this bassist I was telling you about, who began to bring the instruments home. Mr. Kelly, old man Kelly --
Oh, the instruments.
Yeah. He was a professor at the Herron Hill High School.
Was he? And used to let you all take the instruments.
But bass was his favorite. He taught all the instruments, but bass was his love.
Was it?
So that's why we have all those great bassists in Pittsburgh.
Really? Who else? Ray Brown and who else?
Ray Brown, Frank Clarke, and we have another teacher, he's a fantastic bassist, but he never came out to play. He stayed in the public school system with Mr. Kelly.
Really?
Yeah.
A swinging bass player?
Oh, he was a fantastic bass player.
Don't you remember his name?
No, I don't. But he stayed in the school system.
How could a man be content to do that when he -- well, would he go on and jam, or he was older?
No, he would play sometimes.
Yeah.
Let you know, don't be so smart.
That's right.
I'll show you how to play the bass, if you mess around with me. You know one of those kinds of guys.
Yeah. Yeah.
But --
Fancy that. Well, who else?
Well, there was another bass player. I don't know whether Mr. Kelly had anything to do with it, but Ed Safranski (PHONETIC).
Oh, yeah, really?
Yeah, he's from our town too.
Is he?
Yeah. He went to Schenley High School.
Is that right.
So he had to go -- well, he went to Fifth Avenue. It was Fifth Avenue, and then he came to Schenley.
Yeah.
At that time they were playing tubas.
Yeah.
You know?
Yeah. Did your friend Collins play a tuba too?
Frank?
Yeah.

Oh, yeah. Double bass. He would sit it up on the stand with one hand and then play the bass and would put the bass down and play the tuba. Oh, yeah. Musicians were -- oh, they were -- I guess they were much more aware of music, of being a musician then than they are today. I mean because most every musician doubled, he played at least two instruments, like trumpet and this.
Yeah.
Like Benny Carter, I first met Benny Carter in Buffalo with Willie Bryant's band, and he was playing second trumpet in the brass section, and he could outplay all the saxophone players in the band.
Yeah, and I mean he still blows good trumpet.
Yeah, he was fantastic. There were a lot of musicians like that.
